arxiv-2011-09543.title: Travelling waves in the Boussinesq type systems
arxiv-2011-09543.creator: Evgueni Dinvay
arxiv-2011-09543.description: Abstract . Considered herein are a number of variants of the Boussinesq type systems modelling surface water waves. Such equations were derived by different authors to describe the two-way propagation of long gravity waves. A question of existence of special solutions, the so called solitary waves, is of a particular interest.

arxiv-2107-05064.title: The Experimenters’ Dilemma: Inferential Preferences over Populations Thanks: We would like to thank: David Huffman, Sera Linardi, and Lise Vesterlund.
arxiv-2107-05064.creator: Neeraja Gupta, Luca Rigotti, Alistair Wilson
arxiv-2107-05064.description: Abstract . We compare three populations commonly used in experiments by economists and other social scientists: undergraduate students at a physical location (lab), Amazon’s Mechanical Turk (MTurk), and Prolific. The comparison is made along three dimensions: the noise in the data due to inattention, the cost per observation, and the elasticity of response.

arxiv-2107-12327.title: Ionospheric and geomagnetic response to the total solar eclipse on 21 August 2017 Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2107-12327.creator: Amalia Meza, Guillermo Bosch, María Paula Natali, Bernardo Eylenstein
arxiv-2107-12327.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Amalia Meza, Guillermo Bosch, María Paula Natali, Bernardo Eylenstein. Solar eclipses provide an excellent opportunity to study the effects of a sudden localized change in photoionization flux in the Earth’s ionosphere and its consequent repercussion in the Geomagnetic field. We have focused on a subset of the data available from the North American 2017 eclipse in order to study VTEC measurements from GNSS data and geomagnetic field estimations from INTERMAGNET observatories near the eclipse path.

arxiv-2211-10774.title: Emulating Fast Processes in Climate Models
arxiv-2211-10774.creator: Noah D. Brenowitz, W. Andre Perkins, Jacqueline M. Nugent, Oliver Watt-Meyer, Spencer K. Clark, Anna Kwa, Brian Henn, Jeremy McGibbon, Christopher S. Bretherton
arxiv-2211-10774.description: Abstract Cloud microphysical parameterizations in atmospheric models describe the formation and evolution of clouds and precipitation, a central weather and climate process. Cloud-associated latent heating is a primary driver of large and small-scale circulations throughout the global atmosphere, and clouds have important interactions with atmospheric radiation. Clouds are ubiquitous, diverse, and can change rapidly.

arxiv-2307-07033.title: Liquid Thread Breakup and the Formation of Satellite Droplets
arxiv-2307-07033.creator: Luís H. Carnevale, Piotr Deuar, Zhizhao Che, Panagiotis E. Theodorakis*
arxiv-2307-07033.description: Abstract The breakup of liquid threads into smaller droplets is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics. In this study, we estimate the characteristic wavelength of the breakup process by means of many-body dissipative particle dynamics. This wavelength shows a power-law dependence on the Ohnesorge number in line with results from stability analysis.

arxiv-2309-03440.title: Punctate White Matter Lesion Segmentation in Preterm Infants Powered by Counterfactually Generative Learning
arxiv-2309-03440.creator: Zehua Ren, Yongheng Sun, Miaomiao Wang, Yuying Feng, Xianjun Li, Chao Jin, Jian Yang (✉), Chunfeng Lian (✉), Fan Wang (✉)
arxiv-2309-03440.description: Abstract Accurate segmentation of punctate white matter lesions (PWMLs) are fundamental for the timely diagnosis and treatment of related developmental disorders. Automated PWMLs segmentation from infant brain MR images is challenging, considering that the lesions are typically small and low-contrast, and the number of lesions may dramatically change across subjects.

arxiv-2312-00126.title: Positive solutions to semilinear Dirichlet problems with general boundary data Lucian Beznea 1 1 1 Simion Stoilow Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy, P.O. Box 1-764, RO-014700 Bucharest, Romania, and National University of Science and Technology Politehnica Bucharest, CAMPUS Institute.
arxiv-2312-00126.description: Abstract We give a probabilistic representation of the solution to a semilinear elliptic Dirichlet problem with general (discontinuous) boundary data. The boundary behaviour of the solution is in the sense of the controlled convergence initiated by A. Cornea. Uniqueness results for the solution are also provided. Keywords: Semilinear Dirichlet problem, boundary behaviour, controlled convergence.

arxiv-2406-10611.title: Information-theoretic evaluation of covariate distributions models
arxiv-2406-10611.creator: Niklas Hartung, Aleksandra Khatova
arxiv-2406-10611.description: Abstract Statistical modelling of covariate distributions allows to generate virtual populations or to impute missing values in a covariate dataset. Covariate distributions typically have non-Gaussian margins and show nonlinear correlation structures, which simple descriptions like multivariate Gaussian distributions fail to represent.

arxiv-2408-13348.title: Anti-Concentration Inequalities for the Difference of Maxima of Gaussian Random Vectors
arxiv-2408-13348.creator: Alexandre Bellonilabel=e1]abn5@duke.edu, Ethan X. Fanglabel=e2]ethan.fang@duke.edu, Shuting Shenlabel=e3]ss1446@duke.edu
arxiv-2408-13348.description: Abstract We derive novel anti-concentration bounds for the difference between the maximal values of two Gaussian random vectors across various settings. Our bounds are dimension-free, scaling with the dimension of the Gaussian vectors only through the smaller expected maximum of the Gaussian subvectors. In addition, our bounds hold under the degenerate covariance structures, which previous results do not cover.

arxiv-2511-13978.title: Spin-singlet dimer phase in a frustrated square lattice under a magnetic field Journal: Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials
arxiv-2511-13978.creator: L. M. Ramos, M. Schmidt, F. M. Zimmer
arxiv-2511-13978.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by L. M. Ramos, M. Schmidt, F. M. Zimmer. We investigated the isotropic spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} Heisenberg model on an anisotropic square lattice with competing exchange interactions, motivated by the unconventional magnetic behavior observed in the verdazyl-based compound ( o o -MePy-V)PF 6 . Using a cluster mean-field approach, we explore a field-induced phase stabilized by the interplay between frustration and quantum fluctuations, focusing on the role of exchange interactions.

britannica-1911-meilhac-henri.title: Meilhac, Henri (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-meilhac-henri.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-meilhac-henri.description: Article 'Meilhac, Henri' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. born in Paris on the 21st of February 1831, and while a young man began writing fanciful articles for the newspapers and vaudevilles for the theatres, in a vivacious boulevardier spirit which brought him to the front. About 1860 he met Ludovic Halévy, and the two began a collaboration in writing for the stage which lasted for twenty years.

europmc-pmc549063.creator: Romero P, Wagg J, Green ML, Kaiser D, Krummenacker M, Karp PD.
europmc-pmc549063.description: Background We present a computational pathway analysis of the human genome that assigns enzymes encoded therein to predicted metabolic pathways. Pathway assignments place genes in their larger biological context, and are a necessary first step toward quantitative modeling of met

europmc-pmc7082961.title: Astrocyte-derived exosomes enriched with miR-873a-5p inhibit neuroinflammation via microglia phenotype modulation after traumatic brain injury.
europmc-pmc7082961.creator: Long X, Yao X, Jiang Q, Yang Y, He X, Tian W, Zhao K, Zhang H.
europmc-pmc7082961.description: Background The interaction between astrocytes and microglia plays a vital role in the damage and repair of brain lesions due to traumatic brain injury (TBI). Recent studies have shown that exosomes act as potent mediators involved in intercellular communication. Methods In the c

europmc-pmc7143846.title: The Impact of COVID-19 Epidemic Declaration on Psychological Consequences: A Study on Active Weibo Users.

The aim of this study is to explore the impacts of COVID-19 on people's mental health, to assist policy makers to develop actionable policies, and help clinical...

openalex-w7214090581.title: OBESIDADE COMO FATOR DE RISCO PARA O AGRAVAMENTO DO DIABETES MELLITUS TIPO 2: UM ESTUDO ECOLÓGICO

Trata-se de um estudo transversal, observacional e ecológico sobre...

plos-pone-0359628.creator: Muhammad Bilal Riaz, A Zahra, S A Mardan
plos-pone-0359628.description: Physical viability of the massive pulsar PSR J0952–0607 within a polytropic framework

pmc-11509194.title: Biomechanical Analysis of Rectus Femoris Kinesio Taping Effects on Post-Muscle Fatigue Stop-Jump Task Performance
pmc-11509194.creator: Wei-Hsun Tai, Chih-Yu Tu, Chih-Yen Tu, Chen-Fu Huang, Hsien-Te Peng, Kent Doi, Anastassios Philippou, Sergio Hernandez-Sanchez, Juan Cortell-Tormo
pmc-11509194.description: Objectives: This study aims to compare the effects of kinesio tape (KT) on the rectus femoris muscle in athletes and novices under pre- and post-fatigue conditions. Methods: Nineteen male volunteers took part, and fatigue was assessed using the Borg CR10 Scale.

pmc-12431474.title: Enhanced YOLOv8 with DWR-DRB and SPD-Conv for Mechanical Wear Fault Diagnosis in Aero-Engines
pmc-12431474.creator: Qifan Zhou, Bosong Chai, Chenchao Tang, Yingqing Guo, Kun Wang, Xuan Nie, Yun Ye
pmc-12431474.description: Aero-engines, as complex systems integrating numerous rotating components and accessory equipment, operate under harsh and demanding conditions. Prolonged use often leads to frequent mechanical wear and surface defects on accessory parts, which significantly compromise the engine’s normal and stable performance. Therefore, accurately and rigorously identifying failure modes is of critical importance.

pmc-12486599.title: The aesthetic experience of the sublime for a group of Highly Sensitive Persons: Maselli's figurative style vs. Rothko's abstract expressionism
pmc-12486599.creator: Fernando Echarri, Ignacio Miguéliz, Natalia Verea, Teresa Barrio
pmc-12486599.description: Contemporary art museums have become important learning environments to promote visitor aesthetic education. Each piece of art constantly sends different messages to the viewer and creates a person-art connection that can provide significant experiences. These connections can be established in the contemplation of the sublime.

pmc-12575976.title: Progress in the management of pregnancy in patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
pmc-12575976.creator: Yuko Shimizu, Ryotaro Ikeguchi, Kazuo Fujihara, Kenichi Todo
pmc-12575976.description: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is an autoimmune astrocytopathy characterized by autoantibodies against aquaporin-4 (AQP) that predominantly affecting women of childbearing potential. Unlike multiple sclerosis, NMOSD poses a higher risk of severe and irreversible postpartum relapse, making pregnancy a significant concern in affected women.

pmc-12704431.title: Primary gastric squamous cell carcinoma of indeterminate origin managed by laparoscopic multivisceral resection: a case report
pmc-12704431.creator: Luis Osvaldo Suárez Carreón, José Maria Zepeda Torres, Danya Cecilia Muñoz Balderas, Jose Abraham Flores Cardoza, José Víctor Pérez Navarro, Martin Islas Torres, Isac Ismael Ramírez Preciado, Rodrigo Hernández Ramírez, Carlos Francisco Gallegos De Luna, Brian Alejandro Díaz Sandoval, Kevin Kleiman A
pmc-12704431.description: Primary squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the stomach is an exceptionally rare tumor, comprising <0.5% of gastric malignancies. Diagnosis requires strict histopathologic and immunohistochemical confirmation to distinguish it from adenosquamous carcinoma or esophageal extension. We report a 30-year-old woman with chronic anemia and recurrent upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

pmc-12734829.title: From Echo to Coronary Angiography: Optimizing Ischemia Evaluation Through Multimodal Imaging
pmc-12734829.creator: Marija Babic, Lidija Mikic, Marko Ristic, Milorad Tesic, Snezana Tadic, Marija Bjelobrk, Dejana Popovic
pmc-12734829.description: Multimodal imaging plays a central role in optimizing the evaluation and management of myocardial ischemia by leveraging the complementary strengths of echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), positron emission tomography (PET), and invasive coronary angiography (ICA).

pmc-12798931.title: Rethinking Prenatal and Postpartum Exercise
pmc-12798931.creator: Julia Olsen
pmc-12798931.description: Regular physical activity and structured exercise during pregnancy and postpartum are strongly associated with improved maternal and infant health outcomes; however, confusion persists among clinicians, fitness professionals, and patients regarding the safety, intensity, and appropriate modes of exercise across the perinatal period.

pmc-13086954.title: A fast and accurate UV–vis method for the quantification of polylactic acid in biodegradable plastics
pmc-13086954.creator: Sun Min Ji, Tai Gyu Lee
pmc-13086954.description: Polymer blends are used to achieve tailored properties, but the quantification of their components remains difficult. We developed an ultraviolet–visible spectrophotometric method with a two-step pretreatment that involves the conversion of polylactic acid (PLA) into methyl lactate via alcoholysis and then into sodium lactate through alkaline hydrolysis, followed by detection with ferric chloride at wavelengths from 400 to 410 nm.

pmc-13393243.title: Postoperative bisphosphonate therapy is associated with lower prosthesis-related complications after total or reverse shoulder arthroplasty in osteoporotic patients: a TriNetX-based cohort study
pmc-13393243.creator: Wen-Yu Jao, Chih-Cheng Lai, Chi-Sheng Chien, Wen-Shuo Chang
pmc-13393243.description: ObjectivesOsteoporosis is a prevalent comorbidity in patients undergoing total or reverse shoulder arthroplasty and is associated with higher rates of periprosthetic fracture, implant loosening, and revision surgery. While bisphosphonates are commonly used to treat osteoporosis, prior research has primarily examined preoperative use.

pmc-13403830.title: Safety and effects of continuous argatroban administration in acute cerebral infarction: a retrospective analysis
pmc-13403830.creator: Machiko Hirai, Yuki Shigetsura, Daiki Hira, Takakuni Maki, Masayoshi Kawata, Shunsaku Nakagawa, Riki Matsumoto, Tomohiro Terada
pmc-13403830.description: BackgroundArgatroban is an antithrombotic agent commonly used in the acute phase of cerebral infarction. Although the standard administration method is continuous infusion within the first 2 days only, many patients receive continuous intravenous infusion beyond day 3 owing to concerns of symptoms worsening during intermittent dosing, which may be insufficient given the short half-life of argatroban.

pmc-13647403.title: Elevated wzc mutation frequency promotes carbapenem resistance evolution in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae ST23
pmc-13647403.creator: Tao Chen, Xueting Wang, Luying Xiong, Zhuoqi Lou, Ping Lu, Zhien He, Qi Ge, Haoxing Wu, Qixia Luo, Ping Shen, Yunbo Chen, Hui Ding, Yan Geng, Kunpeng Liang, Baorui Yang, Tingting Xiao, Wei Yu, Yonghong Xiao
pmc-13647403.description: The worldwide expansion of carbapenemase-producing hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (CP-hvKP) raises serious concerns about potentially untreatable invasive infections. ST23, an archetypal hvKP clone, has been highlighted due to the rising prevalence of carbapenem resistance largely driven by horizontal plasmid transfer. However, the factors facilitating carbapenemase acquisition in this lineage remained unclear.

uslaw-usc-t17-s905.title: 17 U.S.C. § 905 — Exclusive rights in mask works
uslaw-usc-t17-s905.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t17-s905.description: United States Code, Title 17 (Copyrights); Chapter 9 (Protection Of Semiconductor Chip Products). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The owner of a mask work provided protection under this chapter has the exclusive rights to do and to authorize any of the following: (1) to reproduce the mask work by optical, electronic, or any other means; (2) to import or distribute a semiconductor.
